summary: Changes the policy for the LoST Location Profiles IANA registry from Standards Action to Specification Required, so that standards bodies other than the IETF can add new values.

eli5.summary: Loosens the rules for adding entries to a list, so other standards groups can add their own.

questions: who can add lost location profiles
subtitle: The LoST location profiles registry now takes Specification Required, so bodies like NENA can add values.

tldr.problem: The LoST Location Profiles registry used Standards Action, so every new value needed a Standards Track RFC, yet NENA needed more location profiles.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9036 changes the registry policy to Specification Required and has IANA add the RFC as a reference, with an Expert Reviewer checking each request.
tldr.outcome: Standards bodies other than the IETF can add location profiles.

today: RFC 9036 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5222. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why the Policy Changed
sections.content:
The Location-to-Service Translation (LoST) protocol (RFC 5222) uses a location profile when conveying location, for example in a mapping request and a service boundary result.

RFC 5222 created an IANA registry of profiles under Standards Action, which requires a Standards Track RFC for each new value. The National Emergency Number Association (NENA) uses LoST heavily in its emergency call specifications and identified a need for more profiles.
sections.eli5: Only one big authority could add to the list, but another group needed new entries.

sections.title: The Change
sections.content: RFC 9036 changes the policy of the "Location-to-Service Translation (LoST) Location Profiles" registry from Standards Action to Specification Required, as defined in RFC 8126. This allows standards development organizations other than the IETF to add new values.
sections.eli5: The list now accepts entries backed by a written specification, even from other groups.

sections.title: Expert Review Criteria
sections.content:
IANA changed the registry policy and added this document as a reference. An Expert Reviewer, designated per RFC 8126, should verify three things.

  • The new value is specified by the IETF, NENA or a similar body in which location profiles are in scope.
  • There is a clear need, including that no existing profile meets it.
  • The profile specification is unambiguous and interoperable.
sections.eli5: A checker asks three questions: does a trusted group define it, is it really needed, and is it clearly written?

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: No new security considerations are identified by this change in registry policy. The change only affects who may add entries to the IANA registry.
sections.eli5: Changing who may add to the list does not create a new risk.

references.text: Hardie, T., Newton, A., Schulzrinne, H., and H. Tschofenig, "LoST: A Location-to-Service Translation Protocol", RFC 5222, August 2008.
Cotton, M., Leiba, B., and T. Narten, "Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs", BCP 26, RFC 8126, June 2017.
